turns.content: At a narrow pass, three men in mismatched armor block the road with a felled tree. Their leader says there is a toll: one crate from every wagon.
Brennic steps forward before anyone else can speak, hands loose at his sides. "Toll. For whom? I see no lord's colors. I see three hungry men and a tree, eh, friend?"
The leader's hand drifts toward his sword. He says the lord of this pass is whoever holds it.

"Fair." Brennic nods slowly, copper eyes flicking to the ridge above them, then back. "Then you know the rule. Whoever holds it. We have eleven armed drivers. You have three. And a tree." He lets the silence sit. "Or. A few coins of yellow for your trouble, and you move the tree yourselves."
After a long pause, the leader spits, accepts a small purse, and orders his men to roll the log aside.

Brennic waits until the wagons are well past before he lets his shoulders drop. "Cheaper than burying drivers." He falls in beside the last wagon. "Keep an eye on the ridge for a mile. Men who take a bribe sometimes come back for the rest."
